Subject: Questions on private offer credit structure and channel passback

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement team has started mapping the private offer (AWS Marketplace) terms against our distributor flow and we hit a couple of practical questions on the crediting/"gearing" approach you mentioned. Quick list below — would appreciate concise confirmation so we can feed it to legal/finops: 

1) Is the gearing credit applied against Redwood's marketplace list price (invoice-level) or against our reseller's net (post-passback)? We need to understand where the credit lands for our cost accounting.
2) If we accept an upfront pre-funded credit, can that be amortized monthly on our side, or does marketplace invoicing require a single credit event?
3) For distributor-led resell, what evidence do you need to recognize the channel uplift (reseller margin) so that our distributor can claim the appropriate share?
4) Any constraints on SKU-level packaging for the credit to be eligible (e.g., reserved-capacity SKUs vs on-demand)?

I attached a short list of distributor agreements and our high-level SKU bundle for context (CloudSys_Evidence_Pack.pdf). Also CC'd our procurement mailbox.

Goal: we need a short note we can hand to legal explaining the credit mechanics and what evidence to attach to invoices. Can you get us that by EOD Friday?

Best,
Alyssa Moran

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (Channel Ops) and Naomi (Finance) so we can give a short operational answer + an example. High-level answers below; Ben/Naomi will follow up with the mechanics and evidence checklist: 

1) Short answer: the credit sits at the invoice/list-price layer on the marketplace (Redwood issues an invoice or the marketplace reflects the private offer). The downstream distributor passback is a separate accounting flow — the credit does not automatically reduce the distributor's contracted share unless we explicitly map the passback in the private offer language. In other words: marketplace credit = seller-level credit; distributor netting must be handled by contract routing.

2) Pre-funded credit: we can structure it as a pre-funded bucket (one-time credit on kickoff) or as a usage-triggered credit (monthly reconciliation). The marketplace typically processes the credit event as a settlement line; you can amortize the benefit internally, but the marketplace event will show as a single settlement/credit record unless we break it into recurring credit lines in the offer.

3) Evidence: we need reseller invoices showing the passback calculation or a distributor reconciliation report (monthly) plus a signed reseller acknowledgement of the uplift policy. Ben, see below for the minimal evidence pack he should collect.

4) SKU constraints: reserved/commit SKUs are easiest to map (stable node-hour semantics). On-demand/spot-like SKUs are trickier for gating credits because usage variance complicates reconciliation. If CloudSys prefers reserved SKUs for the private offer, that will simplify both invoicing and passback.

Next steps: Ben will attach a proforma SKU workbook and a short evidence checklist. Naomi will comment on the recommended split (front-loaded vs amortized) from an accounting perspective. If helpful, we can do a 30-minute call tomorrow morning to finalize wording for the PO.

Diego

Alyssa / Diego — attaching the proforma SKU workbook (proforma_skubreakdown.xlsx) and a short sample calc below to make this concrete.

Summary of options (operational):
- Option A: Upfront pre-funded credit (one-time settlement)
  * Redwood posts a settlement credit on the private offer invoice equal to agreed % of list price (e.g., 20% gearing credit).
  * Distributor passback: we require a passback mapping clause that routes X% of the credited amount to distributor netting. Without explicit mapping, distributor revenue share remains calculated off pre-credit invoice amounts.
  * Evidence: distributor monthly reconciliation file + reseller invoice that shows channel passback.

- Option B: Monthly usage-triggered credit (reconciled)
  * Redwood issues monthly settlement credits tied to actual usage lines; easier to align to distributor invoices but increases operational cadence.
  * Evidence: monthly usage export, distributor reconciliation, and PO amendment referencing monthly credits.

Sample calc (simple):
Marketplace list price for SKU-A = $10,000/mo
Agreed gearing credit = 20% => $2,000 credit to CloudSys
Distributor agreed passback = 40% of credit => $800 to distributor, $1,200 retained by CloudSys (or redistributed per your contract)

Notes on mapping: to ensure the distributor receives the passback automatically we need a) explicit passback routing clause in the private offer, or b) a separate credit distribution workflow outside the marketplace (we can automate file drops to your distributor). Most customers prefer (a) to keep bookkeeping simple.

Attached: proforma_skubreakdown.xlsx (contains SKU examples and the calc above across buckets). Also linking our standard distributor-evidence checklist (short) here: https://internal.redwood/ops/channel/evidence-checklist (internal link).

If you want, Diego and I can draft a 2-paragraph clause for the PO that your legal can drop in. Proposed language would specify: credit amount calculation, cadence (one-time vs monthly), and distributor passback percentage and required evidence.

Ben Carter

Thanks everyone — quick finance take and recommended path to minimize month-end reconciliation friction: 

- We prefer Option A (upfront pre-funded credit) but split into two events: 50% at kickoff, 50% after month-3 reconciliation. This reduces the chance of over-crediting against low usage months and keeps the marketplace settlement simple (two credit lines instead of many).
- Required PO language (high level): 
  * Credit schedule (50/50 split) and an explicit call-out that marketplace settlement is at seller invoice level.
  * Distributor passback percentage must be in an appendix to the PO and must be accompanied by monthly reconciliation files (CSV) within 30 days of month-end.
  * Redwood will accept distributor reconciliation as evidence only if it contains the reseller invoice id, SKU mapping, and per-line usage.

Operational asks for CloudSys: please share a point-of-contact at your distributor to receive automated reconciliation files. Also confirm whether you prefer the credit to be applied to reserved SKUs (recommended) or mathed across on-demand SKUs.

If you confirm PO language and distributor contact by EOD Monday our contracts team can produce a short amendment and DocuSign envelope (I can pre-fill the appendix with the passback % once you confirm). Proposed DocuSign link will be sent then: https://www.docusign.com/Envelope/1234-gear-credit-template
